intro.heading: A whole school year, written down as it happens
intro.body: A school year is not a filing job. It is a speech session that quietly ran fifteen minutes instead of thirty, a goal that has said 'some progress' since October, an accommodation nobody has checked since September, and four emails you sent that nobody ever answered. This keeps all of it in one place and does the counting for you — so the difference between the minutes the plan lists and the minutes actually delivered is a number you can read, not a thing you try to remember in a meeting.

privacy.heading: Private by design, not by promise
privacy.body: Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere — it's saved only in this browser, on this device, and it never asks for a Social Security number, account number, Medicaid ID, or password by design. That also means anyone who can use this device and this browser can open it: it isn't encrypted or password-protected, so keep it somewhere only you and whoever else needs it can reach.

cards.title: Zero network requests
cards.body: The app is a single file that runs entirely in your browser, on your device. It makes no connections and loads nothing from the internet. You can run it with Wi-Fi off.

cards.title: Never a password
cards.body: By design, it never asks for or stores passwords or PINs. It records that accounts exist and where your written instructions live — the map, never the keys.

cards.title: Yours forever
cards.body: One-time purchase. The file is yours, works offline for life, and will still open years from now, exactly as it does today.

priceCard.sub: the one private place that carries your child's care through a school year — every service session, every progress report, every request you've made to the school and whether anyone answered — so that when you walk into the annual meeting, the year is already written down.
bullets: 35 guided tasks across seven phases — one Set Up phase, then a school-year spine: Start of the School Year, The First Month Check-In, Every Reporting Period, Around the Breaks, Before the Annual Meeting, and the Letter of Intent
A service delivery log — the minutes the plan lists next to the minutes delivered, with the difference computed for you and totalled across the year
A goal progress log — one row per goal per reporting period, so a year of progress reports reads at a glance instead of from a stack of paper
An accommodations tab — each one, when you last checked, and what you actually saw
A school communication log that tells you how many of your requests are still waiting on an answer
An IEP/504 checklist & meeting log — date, attendees, decisions, and next review date
A providers & therapy tracker — clinicians and this year's school team, with the best way to reach each one
A medication register — dose, prescriber, purpose, last change, and whether this year's school authorization form is on file
A behavioral/incident log — where it happened, what happened, context, and what helped
A benefits tracker — status and renewal dates for SSI, Medicaid waivers, and other programs
A letter-of-intent builder — your child's daily life, who they are, and your hopes for their future
Three one-click printables: a Teacher Sheet for September, a Meeting Prep Sheet for the annual review, and the Caregiver Handoff Packet

faq.a: No. You pay 44.99 once and the app is yours forever. There is no account, no renewal, and nothing that expires.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a: No. You download a small file, double-click it, and it opens in the browser you already use — on Mac, Windows, tablets, and phones.
Yes, structurally. The app makes zero network requests — you can verify this with Wi-Fi turned off. Your entries live only on your device, and your backup is a file you control.

faq.q: What if it doesn't work for me?
faq.a: Email hello@quietkeep.co and we'll make it right. We answer every message.

crossSell.heading: Planning for guardianship too?
crossSell.body: Eleventh Quietkeep organizer and the first in a new ongoing-care lane distinct from the estate and divorce families. The letter of intent reuses the estate line's wishes-engine pattern themed around a child's future, so it cross-sells naturally to the Estate Planning Organizer and Digital Legacy Planner once broader estate and guardianship planning begins, and rhymes with the Caregiving Companion's usage-life shape.
